newsitem.title: INDIA: India asks World Bank to reconsider road project.
newsitem.headline: India asks World Bank to reconsider road project.

text.p: Indian state officials said on Monday they had asked the World Bank to reconsider a decision to abandon an ambitious road and subway project aimed at easing traffic congestion in the commercial capital, Bombay.
"We do hope the Bank will reconsider," a senior official in western Maharashtra, where Bombay is located, told Reuters.
The 35-million-rupee ($978 million) project calls for new roads, additional suburban railway tracks and civic amenities to help reduce congestion in Bombay, one of Asia's most crowded cities.
Almost ten million of Bombay's 13 million residents use the overcrowded city-run bus services and suburban railway network to get to work every day.
But late in March the World Bank warned that it was taking the project off its fund lending programme for the current year because it doubted the government's committment to the project.

"The Bank cannot continue to deploy resources on project preparation if there is no clear evidence of government committment to the project and an institutional framework in place which would permit the project to be implemented effectively and efficiently," it said.
The Bank's decision came six months after its suspension of a $250 million loan to the state-run electricity board because of its dismal financial performance.

A senior World Bank official told Reuters the Bank had spent $1.3 million over the last six years in preliminary work on the project even though a dispute between Indian Railways and the state government had blocked it.
But state officials said they had resolved most of the problems that had troubled the World Bank.

"We have written to the World Bank saying that a good deal of progress has in fact been made towards addressing its concerns," said K. Nalinakshan, the top civil servant in the state's urban development department.
"This is a kind of arm-twisting on their part," he added.
Current World Bank loans to India, through the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, total just over two billion dollars.
